notes: v7 = v6 with one exit change (2026-11-16 22:30 UTC review): the trailing stop on the half kept after the first target is 5% under the best price seen, was 10% (exit.trailing_stop_pct). Why: the bot sees a price every 5 minutes and these tokens often move more than 10% between two readings, so the kept half was sold far under the 10% level: 13.6 points under on average over the 5 real trailing exits (HOGE 14.0 and Rings 16.2 on v6), and on average at a lower price than the half sold at the target. On the recorded snapshots a 5% trail was better or level on each of the 14 replayed trades that reached the first target (11 tokens, worse on none) and, over a buy at any moment, better on 21 to 23 tokens and worse on 5 to 6; a 15% trail was worse. Hints, not findings, and small: about 0.1 point a trade over all trades. It does not make the strategy profitable. v6 = v5 with one universe change, made at Ajeeb's request on 2026-11-16: a token can be traded from 3 hours after launch instead of 3 days (universe.min_age_days 3 to 0.125). His hypothesis: the volume in young tokens is genuine, so a young token with serious buyers and sellers should be considered. Judge young tokens apart (python3 -m bot.report, 'By age of the token at entry'). v5 = v4 with entry.min_txns_h1 150 to 300 (2026-11-16 06:30 UTC review; a signal on a thinly traded token has been reliably bad). Universe and entry are unchanged since v6; portfolio, safety, costs and discovery since v4. See reviews/LESSONS.md for the evidence and what would prove each change wrong. Every threshold is still an untested guess. Change one section at a time and bump 'version' on every edit so trades can be traced to the rules that produced them.
